B06C001.summary: The Kurus, Pandavas and Somakas gather their armies on the plain of Kurukshetra, and Yudhishthira camps on the western side with troops drawn from all of Jamvudwipa. Both sides blow their conches, and then they agree on rules of fair single combat, such as matching opponents by vehicle and never striking those who are unready, fleeing, or unarmed. The chapter sets the stage for the battle and shows the code of conduct the fighters are meant to keep.

scenes.B06C001S01: The two armies assemble at Kurukshetra, the Pandavas make camp and organise their forces, and both sides agree on rules of combat before the fighting begins.

shots.B06C001S01H01: Section heading for the Jamvu-khanda Nirmana Parva.
shots.B06C001S01H02: An opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Saraswati, to be spoken before the telling.
shots.B06C001S01H03: Janamejaya asks how the heroes fought at Kurukshetra.
shots.B06C001S01H04: Vaisampayana begins the account: the Pandavas enter Kurukshetra and camp on the western side, and Yudhishthira provides food, watchwords and badges for the gathered forces from across Jamvudwipa.
shots.B06C001S01H05: Duryodhana arrays his troops, both sides blow their conches amid omens of dust and flesh-and-blood showers, and the warriors agree on rules of fair combat.

B06C002.summary: Vyasa, seeing the two armies ready to fight, takes the distressed Dhritarashtra aside and offers to let him watch the battle. Dhritarashtra says he does not want to see his kinsmen slaughtered and asks only to hear about it, so Vyasa grants the bard Sanjaya, son of Gavalgani, the power to see and narrate the whole war. Vyasa then lists frightening omens in the sky and on earth that foreshadow terrible losses.

scenes.B06C002S01: Vyasa speaks privately with Dhritarashtra, gives Sanjaya the power to report the battle, and describes the omens of disaster he sees around the field.

shots.B06C002S01H01: Vyasa sees the armies drawn up for battle and speaks privately to the grieving Dhritarashtra about his sons' wrongdoing.
shots.B06C002S01H02: Vyasa tells the king that his sons and the other princes have reached their appointed hour and will kill one another, and offers to give him sight so he can watch.
shots.B06C002S01H03: Dhritarashtra replies that he does not want to see his kinsmen slaughtered, but asks to hear a full account of the fighting.
shots.B06C002S01H04: Vyasa grants Sanjaya celestial sight and hearing, freedom from weapons and fatigue, and says the fame of the Kurus and Pandavas will spread, and that victory lies with righteousness.
shots.B06C002S01H05: Vyasa warns of a great slaughter and lists omens: birds and beasts gathering to feed on the field, strange sights in the sun and moon, eerie cries, and weeping animals.

B06C003.summary: Vyasa lists more portents, including monstrous births, unseasonal crops, planetary disturbances, eclipses on unusual days and bloody rivers, all forecasting a massacre. Dhritarashtra accepts that the slaughter is fated, but Vyasa urges him to restrain his sons and let the Pandavas have their kingdom, and Dhritarashtra admits his sons will not obey him. Dhritarashtra then asks what signs will show that a side is destined to win, and Vyasa lists omens of success and says that victory depends on chance.

scenes.B06C003S01: Vyasa lists portents of a coming slaughter and urges Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons, and Dhritarashtra replies that he is powerless over them.
scenes.B06C003S02: Dhritarashtra asks about the signs of victory, and Vyasa describes them, warning about panic in an army and the uncertainty of war.

shots.B06C003S01H01: Vyasa lists monstrous births, odd plant growth, planetary disturbances, eclipses on unusual days, and bloody rivers and winds as portents of a great slaughter.
shots.B06C003S01H02: Dhritarashtra says he thinks all this was ordained long ago, and that kings who die fighting by the duties of their order will win heaven and fame.
shots.B06C003S01H03: Vyasa says Time both destroys and creates the world, urges Dhritarashtra to show his sons the path of righteousness, and asks him to let the Pandavas have their kingdom.
shots.B06C003S01H04: Dhritarashtra replies that he understands life and death as well as Vyasa does, but people lose their judgement where their own interests are concerned, and his sons do not obey him.
shots.B06C003S01H05: Vyasa invites Dhritarashtra to speak freely about what is on his mind so that he can remove his doubts.
shots.B06C003S02H01: Dhritarashtra asks Vyasa to describe the indications that come before victory in battle.
shots.B06C003S02H02: Vyasa lists signs of success, such as a clear fire, pleasant sounds and favourable birds, explains how panic spreads through an army, ranks success by negotiation highest and success by battle lowest, and concludes that victory depends on chance.

B06C004.summary: After Vyasa leaves, Dhritarashtra sighs over the many kings gathered to kill one another and asks Sanjaya to describe the lands they came from. Sanjaya sorts living things into mobile and immobile, lists the fourteen kinds of animals and the plants, and says all creatures live by consuming one another. He concludes that the earth sustains everything, which is why kings kill each other to possess it.

scenes.B06C004S01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to describe the lands from which the armies came, and Sanjaya explains the kinds of living things and why the earth is worth fighting over.

shots.B06C004S01H01: Vyasa leaves, Dhritarashtra falls silent and sighs, and then asks Sanjaya to describe the lands and cities from which the assembled kings and their troops came.
shots.B06C004S01H02: Sanjaya sorts living things into mobile and immobile, lists the wild and domestic animals and the kinds of plants, and says the earth is the support of all creatures, which is why kings kill one another for it.

B06C005.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya for the names and measures of the rivers, mountains, provinces and forests on the earth. Sanjaya first explains that all things are made from five elements, each with its own quality, and that the earth holds the qualities of the others as well. He then describes the wheel-shaped island Sudarsana, which he says resembles a peepul tree and a hare when seen in the moon.

scenes.B06C005S01: Dhritarashtra asks for a survey of the earth, and Sanjaya explains the five elements and then describes the island Sudarsana.

shots.B06C005S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to name and measure the rivers, mountains, provinces and forests on the earth.
shots.B06C005S01H02: Sanjaya explains that all things are built from five elements, each with its own quality, and that some matters are beyond reason to work out.
shots.B06C005S01H03: Sanjaya describes the wheel-shaped island Sudarsana, with its rivers, mountains, cities and trees, ringed by the salt ocean, and its shape as seen in the moon.

B06C006.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya for more detail on the hare-shaped and peepul-shaped parts of the island. Sanjaya describes the six mountains that cross the land, the Varshas between them, and the golden mountain Meru at the centre with its surrounding islands, including Jamvudwipa where the listeners live. He covers the sacred places, the course of the Ganga and the lives of gods, sages and peoples around these mountains, which sets out the world in which the Kurus fight.

scenes.B06C006S01: Sanjaya lays out the mountains, lands and sacred places of the world, starting with the mountains that divide it and ending with the hare-shaped region.

shots.B06C006S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks for a fuller account of the island, beginning with the hare-shaped part and then the peepul-shaped part.
shots.B06C006S01H02: Vaisampayana says that the king's request prompted Sanjaya to begin.
shots.B06C006S01H03: Sanjaya names the six mountains that cross the land, the Varshas between them, the golden mountain Meru at the centre, and the sacred places, rivers and peoples on and around it.
shots.B06C006S01H04: Sanjaya sums up the seven Varshas and says the islands Naga-dwipa and Kasyapa-dwipa and the mountains of Maleya form the parts of the hare-shaped region.

B06C007.summary: Dhritarashtra asks about the regions north and east of Meru and the Malyavat mountain. Sanjaya describes the Northern Kurus, a land of sweet fruit, milk-giving trees, golden sands and long-lived people, then the eastern land of Bhadraswa with its great Kalamra and Jamvu trees, which gave Jamvudwipa its name. He ends with Malyavat, where the fire Samvataka burns at the end of an age and ascetics enter the sun and then the moon.

scenes.B06C007S01: Sanjaya describes the Northern Kurus, the eastern land of Bhadraswa with its great trees, and the mountain Malyavat with its fire and its ascetics.

shots.B06C007S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks for a detailed account of the regions north and east of Meru and of the mountains of Malyavat.
shots.B06C007S01H02: Sanjaya describes the Northern Kurus, with fruit and flowers that grow to order, milk-giving trees, golden sands, twins born there, long lives, and birds that carry off the dead.
shots.B06C007S01H03: Sanjaya describes Bhadraswa, its Kalamra tree whose juice keeps people youthful, and the Jamvu tree whose name gave this island its name, along with the river and gold that flow from it.
shots.B06C007S01H04: Sanjaya describes Malyavat, where the fire Samvataka burns at the end of an age, and the golden-hued ascetics who enter the sun and later the moon.

B06C008.summary: Dhritarashtra asks for the names of all the Varshas, mountains and their inhabitants. Sanjaya lists Romanaka, Hiranmaya and the Airavata Varsha beyond the Sringavat mountains, with their long-lived peoples, and describes Hari (Vishnu) riding a golden car in the northern ocean as the source and end of all creatures. Dhritarashtra, lost in thought about his sons, answers that Time both destroys and creates everything and names Narayana and Vishnu as the power that destroys all creatures.

scenes.B06C008S01: Sanjaya lists the remaining Varshas and their mountains and peoples, and Dhritarashtra reflects on Time and on the power of Vishnu.

shots.B06C008S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to name every Varsha and mountain, and every being that dwells on them.
shots.B06C008S01H02: Sanjaya describes Romanaka, Hiranmaya with its river and the eagle Garuda, the Sringavat mountains, the Airavata Varsha where the sun gives no heat, and the god Hari on his golden car.
shots.B06C008S01H03: Dhritarashtra, absorbed in thought about his sons, says that Time destroys and creates the universe and names Nara and Narayana, also called Vaikuntha and Vishnu, as the power that destroys creatures.

B06C009.summary: Dhritarashtra asks about Bharatavarsha, the land his son Duryodhana covets, and Sanjaya replies that the Pandavas do not covet it, while Duryodhana, Sakuni and other rulers do. He then names the mountains, rivers and many peoples and provinces of the land and of the south and north. He ends by saying kings have become greedy for earth like dogs fighting over meat, which is why the Kurus and Pandavas strive for it.

scenes.B06C009S01: Dhritarashtra asks about Bharatavarsha, Sanjaya blames Duryodhana for the greed over it, and he gives long lists of its mountains, rivers and peoples before explaining why kings fight over earth.

shots.B06C009S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to describe Bharatavarsha, the land that his son covets, that the sons of Pandu also want, and that troubles his own mind.
shots.B06C009S01H02: Sanjaya says the Pandavas are not greedy for the land, names the kings who are, and then describes the land's ancient royal lovers, its seven Kala mountains, and the many rivers that feed it.
shots.B06C009S01H03: Sanjaya lists the provinces and peoples of the land, a long catalogue of kingdoms and tribes.
shots.B06C009S01H04: Sanjaya lists the kingdoms of the south and the north and compares the earth to a cow that yields virtue, profit and pleasure, and says that kings grasp greedily for it, so the Kurus and Pandavas are fighting over it by negotiation, division, gift and battle.

B06C010.summary: Dhritarashtra asks about the lifespan, strength and condition of the people of Bharatavarsha, Himavat and Harivarsha. Sanjaya explains the four ages, Krita, Treta, Dwapara and Kali, and how lifespans shrink from four thousand years to an uncertain span, while human character declines in the Kali age. He concludes that Haimavat and Harivarsha are superior to Bharatavarsha in every quality.

scenes.B06C010S01: Dhritarashtra asks about the people of the neighbouring lands, and Sanjaya explains the four ages and how the people of each age differ.

shots.B06C010S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks for a detailed account of the lifespan, strength and good and bad conditions of people in Bharatavarsha, Himavat and Harivarsha, past, present and future.
shots.B06C010S01H02: Sanjaya explains the four ages, their lifespans, the strength and wisdom of people in each age, the decline in character in the Kali age, and ranks Haimavat and Harivarsha above Bharatavarsha.

B06C011.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya for the size of Jamvudwipa and the oceans and islands beyond it, including Sakadwipa, Kusadwipa, Salmalidwipa and Kraunchadwipa, along with the sun, moon and Rahu. Sanjaya describes Sakadwipa, an island twice the size of Jamvudwipa where people are righteous and do not die, and then names its seven mountains, the Varshas between them, and the sacred Saka tree. The account gives the king a cosmic map of the world beyond his own land.

scenes.B06C011S01: The Bhumi Parva opens with Dhritarashtra's request for the size of Jamvudwipa and its neighbouring islands, and Sanjaya describes Sakadwipa.
scenes.B06C011S02: Sanjaya names the seven mountains of Sakadwipa, their Varshas and rivers, the Saka tree and the four peaceful provinces, and Dhritarashtra asks why the people there are dark.

shots.B06C011S01H01: Section heading for the Bhumi Parva.
shots.B06C011S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks for the size of Jamvudwipa, the oceans and islands of Sakadwipa, Kusadwipa, Salmalidwipa and Kraunchadwipa, and the planets Rahu, Soma and Surya.
shots.B06C011S01H03: Sanjaya says he will describe seven islands, gives the extent of the Jamvu mountain, and says the salt ocean around it is twice that size and filled with kingdoms and mountains.
shots.B06C011S01H04: Sanjaya describes Sakadwipa, twice the size of Jamvudwipa and surrounded by its own ocean, where people are righteous and never die, and asks what more the king wishes to hear.
shots.B06C011S01H05: Dhritarashtra asks for a full, detailed account of Sakadwipa.
shots.B06C011S02H01: Sanjaya names the island's seven jewelled mountains, starting with Meru, and describes Malaya, Jaladhara, Raivataka and Syama, noting how their clouds, rain and constellation Revati are linked to them.
shots.B06C011S02H02: Dhritarashtra asks why the people of Sakadwipa would be dark-skinned.
shots.B06C011S02H03: Sanjaya answers that people of all complexions live on islands, names the Dark Mountain after its dark people, lists the rest of the mountains, Varshas and rivers, the Saka tree, and the four provinces where people live peacefully by their castes.

B06C012.summary: Sanjaya describes the northern islands, each surrounded by an ocean of clarified butter, curds, wine or water, with their mountains, Varshas and long-lived, peaceful peoples. He covers the outer islands and Pushkara where Prajapati dwells, and the four great elephants whose breath gives life to creatures. He ends with the sizes of the planet Swarbhanu, the moon and the sun, urges Dhritarashtra to pacify Duryodhana, and closes by saying that hearing this Bhumi Parva brings merit.

scenes.B06C012S01: Sanjaya describes the outer islands and their oceans, mountains and peoples, then the heavenly bodies, and closes with advice to Dhritarashtra and the merit of hearing the Bhumi Parva.

shots.B06C012S01H01: Sanjaya describes the oceans of clarified butter, curds, wine and water, the northern islands and their mountains, and the Varshas whose people are almost white and never die.
shots.B06C012S01H02: Sanjaya describes the remaining islands and mountains, the realms where Prajapati rules, and the four great elephants whose breath gives life to creatures.
shots.B06C012S01H03: Dhritarashtra says Sanjaya has described the first subject fully and asks him to go on to what remains.
shots.B06C012S01H04: Sanjaya gives the sizes of the planet Swarbhanu, the moon and the sun, explains that Rahu eclipses them, and urges Dhritarashtra to pacify his son Duryodhana.
shots.B06C012S01H05: Closing passage: a Kshatriya who hears this Bhumi Parva gains prosperity, and hearing it on full-moon or new-moon days brings blessings to the hearer and to ancestors.

B06C013.summary: Sanjaya rushes back from the battlefield and tells the grieving Dhritarashtra that Bhishma, the grandsire of the Bharatas, has been slain by Sikhandin and lies on a bed of arrows. He recalls Bhishma's great feats and his long resistance against the Pandavas, and blames the king's evil counsel for the disaster. The news marks a turning point, since Bhishma had been the mainstay of the Kaurava army.

scenes.B06C013S01: Sanjaya enters the court and announces that Bhishma has fallen, recalling his greatness and blaming Dhritarashtra's evil counsel.

shots.B06C013S01H01: Section heading for the Bhagavat-Gita Parva.
shots.B06C013S01H02: Vaisampayana says that Sanjaya, who knows past, present and future, rushes in grief to tell Dhritarashtra, who is lost in thought, that Bhishma has been slain.
shots.B06C013S01H03: Sanjaya announces Bhishma's death, recalls his feats and his long resistance, says he now lies on a bed of arrows struck down by Sikhandin, and blames the king's evil counsel.

B06C014.summary: Dhritarashtra, stunned, asks how Bhishma could have been killed by Sikhandin, who protected him, and how the Pandavas overcame him. He calls his own heart as hard as adamant for not breaking, and fears for the outcome now that the army has lost its foremost warrior. He demands every detail of the battle, saying he cannot regain his composure without it.

scenes.B06C014S01: Dhritarashtra, overwhelmed with grief, asks a long series of questions about how Bhishma fell, who protected him, and what his sons and allies did, and he begs Sanjaya to tell him everything.

shots.B06C014S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks how Bhishma was slain by Sikhandin, who followed and protected him, which heroes opposed the Pandavas, and laments his own wicked counsel and the fall of his protector.
shots.B06C014S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks how the Pandavas overcame Bhishma, what Duryodhana, Karna, Sakuni and Dussasana said when he fell, and who won and who was lost, and begs Sanjaya to tell him everything in detail.

B06C016.summary: After the night passes, the kings shout Array! and the armies rise and take their positions at dawn. Sanjaya describes the great show of banners, chariots and warriors, the Kaurava commanders such as Sakuni, Salya and Jayadratha who each lead an Akshauhini, and Bhishma in white at the head of the Kaurava vanguard. He ends by comparing the two armies to oceans at the end of an age.

scenes.B06C016S01: At dawn both armies take their positions, Sanjaya lists the Kaurava commanders and Bhishma at the front, and he compares the two armies to great oceans.

shots.B06C016S01H01: Sanjaya describes the din and the dawn arrangement of both armies, the glittering weapons and banners, the Kaurava commanders, Bhishma leading the vanguard in white, the Pandava divisions, and the two armies compared to oceans at the end of an age.

B06C015.summary: Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra not to blame Duryodhana, since men bring evil upon themselves by their own misdeeds, and recalls that the Pandavas long bore their injuries in the woods. He then says that the events were predestined and that he now has divine sight and hearing, granted through Vyasa, to report them. He recounts Duryodhana's orders to protect Bhishma at all costs, as Bhishma had vowed not to strike Sikhandin, and the guards Duryodhana names on the Pandava side.

scenes.B06C015S01: Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra not to blame Duryodhana, describes his divine sight, and recounts Duryodhana's orders to protect Bhishma from Sikhandin.

shots.B06C015S01H01: Sanjaya says the question is fair but the king should not blame Duryodhana for the consequences of his own misdeeds, and recalls the Pandavas long bore their injuries in the woods.
shots.B06C015S01H02: Sanjaya says the events were predestined, that Vyasa has given him divine sight and hearing, and that he will now describe the battle between the Bharatas.
shots.B06C015S01H03: Duryodhana tells Dussasana to send cars and troops to protect Bhishma, repeats Bhishma's vow not to strike Sikhandin, and names the Pandava guards around Arjuna.
shots.B06C015S01H04: Section heading marking the start of Section XVI.

B06C017.summary: Sanjaya describes the first day of the great battle, with ominous signs in the sky and the kings assembling as Vyasa had foretold. Bhishma urges the kings to fight bravely, since death in battle is a Kshatriya's duty and leads to heaven, and Karna alone lays down his weapons out of respect for him. The Kaurava divisions then advance under their named leaders, and their great formation is described in detail.

scenes.B06C017S01: On the first day, Bhishma urges the kings to fight, Karna lays down his arms, the Kaurava divisions advance under their leaders, and their battle formation is set out.

shots.B06C017S01H01: Sanjaya describes the ominous signs at the start of battle, the kings assembling as Vyasa foretold, Bhishma's exhortation to the kings to fight for heaven, Karna laying down his arms for Bhishma's sake, the Kaurava divisions and their leaders, and their formation shaped like a body of elephants, kings and horses.

B06C018.summary: The field fills with uproar, banners and glittering armour as the two armies face each other. Sanjaya lists the Kaurava warriors who guard Bhishma from behind, the peoples pledged to fight to the death, and the huge forces of foot soldiers and chariots. He sums up the Kaurava army of eleven Akshauhinis as a great river divided.

scenes.B06C018S01: The armies clash in uproar and display, and Sanjaya lists the warriors and peoples who guard Bhishma and the size of the Kaurava force.

shots.B06C018S01H01: Sanjaya describes the uproar, the glittering standards and armour, the Kaurava warriors who guard Bhishma from behind, the peoples pledged to fight to the death, the huge forces of chariots, elephants and foot soldiers, and the eleven Akshauhinis compared with a river divided.

B06C019.summary: Dhritarashtra asks how Yudhishthira could form a counter-array against Bhishma's great army with fewer troops. Sanjaya reports that Yudhishthira cites a precept of Vrihaspati for few against many, and Arjuna proposes the Vajra array, with Bhima at the front and the other Pandava warriors and allies placed around him, Sikhandin facing Bhishma, and Yudhishthira in the centre. Dawn then brings wind, dust, thunder and falling meteors, which the sons of Pandu face calmly.

scenes.B06C019S01: Yudhishthira asks Arjuna for a formation, Arjuna sets out the Vajra array, and omens of wind, dust and thunder appear at dawn.

shots.B06C019S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks how Yudhishthira countered the Kaurava array with fewer men, and how the Pandavas set against Bhishma, who knows every kind of formation.
shots.B06C019S01H02: Yudhishthira cites Vrihaspati's advice that few against many should use a needle-shaped array, and Arjuna answers with the Vajra array, placing Bhima at the front, the other warriors and allies around him, Sikhandin facing Bhishma, and Yudhishthira in the centre.
shots.B06C019S01H03: At dawn, wind, drops of water, dry gusts, dust, falling meteors and a dimmed sun appear, and the Pandava army stands ready with Bhima at its head.

B06C020.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya which side was eager to fight first and which side the omens favoured. Sanjaya says both armies were equally joyful and grand, with the Kauravas facing west and the Pandavas facing east, and the wind blowing against the Kauravas. He describes the Kaurava positions, with Duryodhana in the centre, Bhishma at the front in white, Drona at the rear and other leaders in their places, and says the Pandava army seemed invincible because Krishna and Arjuna led it.

scenes.B06C020S01: Dhritarashtra asks which side was eager and which had the omens, and Sanjaya describes both armies, the omens and the Kaurava commanders.

shots.B06C020S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks which army first advanced eagerly, which side the sun, moon and wind favoured, which beasts cried out inauspiciously, and which young men looked cheerful.
shots.B06C020S01H02: Sanjaya says both armies were equally joyful and vast, describes the facing directions, the omens against the Kauravas, the Kaurava leaders and their places, and says the Pandava army seemed invincible because Krishna and Arjuna led it.

B06C021.summary: Seeing Bhishma's impenetrable array, Yudhishthira grows pale and asks Arjuna how the few can hope to beat the many. Arjuna replies that victory comes through truth, compassion, righteousness and energy rather than sheer might, and that victory is wherever Krishna is. He backs this with the old story of the gods' victory through Hari's grace.

scenes.B06C021S01: Yudhishthira is dismayed by Bhishma's array, and Arjuna answers that victory lies with righteousness and with Krishna.

shots.B06C021S01H01: Yudhishthira, dismayed at Bhishma's array, asks Arjuna how the Pandavas can win, and Arjuna replies that victory comes from truth, righteousness and energy, and that it is with Krishna, recalling how the gods won through Hari's grace.

B06C022.summary: Yudhishthira sets the Pandava forces in counter-array and urges them to fight fairly and seek the highest heaven. Sanjaya describes the commanders in their places, Arjuna's car drawn by white horses and driven by Krishna, and Bhima leading the van. Krishna then points out Bhishma standing in the midst of his army and urges Arjuna to attack him.

scenes.B06C022S01: Yudhishthira arranges the Pandava army and urges it to fight fairly, Sanjaya describes the commanders and Arjuna's car, and Krishna points out Bhishma and urges Arjuna to attack him.

shots.B06C022S01H01: Yudhishthira arranges the Pandava army and urges it to fight fairly, places Sikhandin at the centre with Arjuna guarding him, Dhrishtadyumna in the van with Bhima, Yuyudhana on the south, and himself among the elephants with priests blessing him, and Sanjaya describes Arjuna's car and Bhima's terrifying strength.
shots.B06C022S01H02: Krishna, driving Arjuna's car, tells Arjuna that Bhishma stands in the midst of his troops, surrounded by great warriors, and urges him to seek battle with that bull of the Bharatas.

B06C023.summary: As the Kaurava army approaches, Krishna tells Arjuna to purify himself and recite a hymn to Durga for victory. Arjuna dismounts and recites a long hymn praising the goddess by many names, and she appears in the sky and promises that he will soon defeat his foes with Narayana's help. The chapter ends with Krishna and Arjuna blowing their conches and with a list of the protections that reciting the hymn brings.

scenes.B06C023S01: Krishna urges Arjuna to pray to Durga, and Arjuna recites a long hymn to the goddess before the battle.
scenes.B06C023S02: Durga appears and promises Arjuna victory, Krishna and Arjuna blow their conches, and Sanjaya explains the benefits of the hymn and the reason for victory.

shots.B06C023S01H01: Sanjaya notes that Krishna speaks to Arjuna as the Kaurava army comes forward to fight.
shots.B06C023S01H02: Krishna tells Arjuna to purify himself and recite a hymn to Durga on the eve of battle for victory.
shots.B06C023S01H03: Arjuna dismounts from his car and joins his hands to recite the hymn.
shots.B06C023S01H04: Arjuna's long hymn calls on Durga by many names and epithets, and describes her as the power behind sleep, prosperity, the sun and the moon, and the protector of those who worship her.
shots.B06C023S01H05: Sanjaya says that Durga, pleased by Arjuna's devotion, appears in the sky in Krishna's presence and speaks.
shots.B06C023S02H01: Durga tells Arjuna that he will soon defeat his foes, that Narayana is with him, and that no enemy, not even Indra, can defeat him.
shots.B06C023S02H02: The goddess vanishes, Arjuna mounts his car, and Krishna and Arjuna blow their celestial conches, and the hymn is said to bring protection, safety and success to whoever recites it at dawn.
shots.B06C023S02H03: Sanjaya says he knows this through Vyasa's grace, that Dhritarashtra's sons do not know Nara and Narayana, that the hour of the kingdom has come, and that victory goes where righteousness and Krishna are.

B06C024.summary: Dhritarashtra asks who advanced cheerfully, who struck the first blow, and whose troops were in higher spirits. Sanjaya replies that both armies were equally cheerful and fragrant, and that the collision was fierce, with music, conches, drums and roars.

scenes.B06C024S01: Dhritarashtra asks who began the fight in high spirits, and Sanjaya says that both armies were equally eager and the clash was fierce.

shots.B06C024S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya which side advanced in confidence, which side struck first, and whose troops were praised with fragrance and fierce words.
shots.B06C024S01H02: Sanjaya says both armies were equally cheerful and fragrant, and describes the fierce collision with music, conches, drums, roars and elephant grunts.

B06C025.summary: The Bhagavad Gita opens as Dhritarashtra asks what his sons and the Pandavas did on the plain of Kurukshetra. Sanjaya reports that Duryodhana names the Pandava warriors and his own leaders to Drona, the conches sound, and Arjuna asks Krishna to drive his car between the armies. Krishna does so, Arjuna sees his kinsmen on both sides, and he sinks into grief, lays down his bow and sits down in his car.

scenes.B06C025S01: The Gita opens as Dhritarashtra asks about the armies, Duryodhana names the leaders on both sides, the conches sound, and Arjuna asks to see the warriors before battle.
scenes.B06C025S02: Krishna places Arjuna's car between the armies, Arjuna sees his kinsmen, and he is overcome with grief, lays down his bow and sits down in his car.

shots.B06C025S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter I.
shots.B06C025S01H02: An editor's note by John Bruno Hare says the Gita proper begins here, and that the chapter headings were added for comparison and are not in Ganguli's original.
shots.B06C025S01H03: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what his sons and the Pandavas did after assembling on the sacred plain of Kurukshetra.
shots.B06C025S01H04: Duryodhana tells Drona that the Pandava army is strong, names the Pandava and Kaurava warriors, says his own army protected by Bhishma is insufficient, and then the conches sound on both sides.
shots.B06C025S01H05: Arjuna asks Krishna to place his car between the two armies so that he can see the warriors who are ready to fight.
shots.B06C025S02H01: Krishna places the car between the armies, and Arjuna sees his fathers, grandfathers, teachers, relatives and friends standing on both sides.
shots.B06C025S02H02: Arjuna, overcome with pity, describes his trembling and dry mouth, says he wants neither victory nor kingdom, and argues that killing his own family destroys its customs and brings sin and disorder.
shots.B06C025S02H03: Sanjaya says Arjuna, troubled with grief, casts aside his bow and arrows and sits down on his car.
shots.B06C025S02H04: A closing editorial note marks the end of the first lesson of the Gita, titled Survey of Forces, within the Bhishma Parva.

B06C026.summary: Arjuna, overcome with pity, lays down his weapons and refuses to fight his teachers and kin, and Krishna rebukes his weakness. Krishna then teaches that the soul is eternal and cannot be killed, that a warrior should fight a just battle as his duty, and that one should act without attachment to the results. He ends by describing the steady-minded sage who is content within and free from desire, fear and anger.

scenes.B06C026S01: Arjuna, overcome with grief, refuses to fight, and Krishna rebukes him for his weakness.
scenes.B06C026S02: Krishna teaches that the soul is eternal, that a warrior must fight his just battle without attachment to results, and describes the steady-minded sage.

shots.B06C026S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter II.
shots.B06C026S01H02: Sanjaya says that Krishna, the slayer of Madhu, speaks to the despairing Arjuna whose eyes are filled with tears.
shots.B06C026S01H03: Krishna asks where this unworthy weakness has come from, tells Arjuna that it shuts out heaven and brings disgrace, and urges him to shake it off and rise to fight.
shots.B06C026S01H04: Arjuna asks how he can fight with arrows against Bhishma and Drona, his worthy teachers, says that begging would be better than killing them, admits he does not know which outcome is better, and asks Krishna to instruct him as a disciple.
shots.B06C026S01H05: Sanjaya reports that Arjuna declares he will not fight and falls silent, and that Krishna then speaks to him between the two armies.
shots.B06C026S02H01: Krishna answers that the wise grieve neither for the living nor the dead, since the soul is eternal, cannot be slain, and simply changes bodies, so Arjuna should fight his just battle as a warrior and act without attachment to results.
shots.B06C026S02H02: Arjuna asks what marks a person of steady mind, and how such a person speaks, sits and moves.
shots.B06C026S02H03: Krishna describes the steady sage as one who is content within, untroubled by calamity, free from desire, fear and anger, who withdraws his senses as a tortoise draws in its limbs, and who attains peace.

B06C027.summary: Arjuna asks why Krishna praises devotion through knowledge yet urges him to dreadful action, and Krishna answers that no one escapes action by refraining from it. He teaches that one should act without attachment, as an offering, and gives the examples of the Lord of creation and of himself, who acts to keep the world in order. Krishna then names desire, born of passion, as the great enemy that drives people to sin and must be conquered.

scenes.B06C027S01: Arjuna asks why he must act, Krishna teaches action without attachment as sacrifice, and then names desire as the enemy that must be overcome.

shots.B06C027S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter III.
shots.B06C027S01H02: Arjuna asks why Krishna praises devotion yet urges him to dreadful action, and asks for a plain answer about what is good for him.
shots.B06C027S01H03: Krishna explains that there are two paths, knowledge and work, that no one escapes action by refraining from it, and that one should act without attachment as an offering, citing the Lord of creation, Janaka, and his own example of acting to keep the world in order; he adds that one's own duty, however imperfect, is better than another's.
shots.B06C027S01H04: Arjuna asks what drives a person to sin even against his will.
shots.B06C027S01H05: Krishna answers that desire, born of passion and turned to wrath, is the all-devouring enemy that covers knowledge like smoke covers fire, and urges Arjuna to restrain his senses and destroy it.

B06C028.summary: Krishna says he first taught this imperishable path to Vivaswat, who passed it to Manu and Ikshaku, and that it was lost over time until he gave it again to Arjuna. Arjuna asks how this can be, since Vivaswat was born before Krishna, and Krishna answers that he is unborn yet appears in every age to protect righteousness. He then explains action without craving, the many kinds of sacrifice, and says that the sacrifice of knowledge burns away all action, urging Arjuna to cut his doubt with it.

scenes.B06C028S01: Krishna explains how this teaching was passed down, answers Arjuna's question about his births, and teaches action, sacrifice and knowledge before urging Arjuna to cast off doubt.

shots.B06C028S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter IV.
shots.B06C028S01H02: Krishna says he declared this imperishable teaching first to Vivaswat, that it passed through Manu and Ikshaku, that it was lost over time, and that he now gives it to Arjuna as his devotee and friend.
shots.B06C028S01H03: Arjuna points out that Vivaswat was born before Krishna and asks how Krishna could have taught it first.
shots.B06C028S01H04: Krishna says he has taken many births that Arjuna does not remember, appears in each age to protect the righteous, explains action done without craving, the many kinds of sacrifice, and that the sacrifice of knowledge burns away all action; he urges Arjuna to learn from wise teachers and cut his doubt with the sword of knowledge.

B06C029.summary: Arjuna asks whether giving up action or acting with devotion is the better path, and Krishna answers that both lead to freedom but that acting with devotion is superior. He says the wise see the two paths as one, and that a person who acts without attachment, offering the fruit to Brahman, is untouched by sin. The chapter closes with the portrait of the sage who is at peace, equal toward all beings, and who knows Krishna as the enjoyer of sacrifice.

scenes.B06C029S01: Arjuna asks which is better, renunciation or action, and Krishna explains that acting with devotion is superior and describes the sage who is at peace.

shots.B06C029S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter V.
shots.B06C029S01H02: Arjuna asks Krishna which is superior, giving up actions or taking them up with devotion, and asks for a definite answer.
shots.B06C029S01H03: Krishna says both paths lead to freedom but acting with devotion is better, that the wise see the two as one, that acting without attachment and offering it to Brahman leaves a person untouched by sin, and that the sage who is at peace and equal to all beings attains tranquillity, knowing Krishna as the enjoyer of sacrifices.

B06C030.summary: Krishna explains that a true renouncer does what is required without seeking the fruit, and he describes the practice of meditation, including posture, moderation in food and sleep, and steady attention on him. Arjuna protests that the restless mind is as hard to control as the wind, and Krishna replies that practice and detachment can tame it. Krishna then assures Arjuna that a devotee who falls short is not lost, and that the one who worships him with faith is the most devout.

scenes.B06C030S01: Krishna describes the true renouncer and the practice of meditation, and he and Arjuna discuss how hard it is to still the restless mind.
scenes.B06C030S02: Krishna says the devotee who falls away is not lost, and that the one who worships him with faith is the most devout.

shots.B06C030S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter VI.
shots.B06C030S01H02: Krishna says that true renunciation means doing required actions without seeking their fruit, then describes meditation: a steady seat in a clean place, a still body, the gaze fixed at the nose tip, moderation in food and sleep, the mind fixed on him, and the devotee who sees himself in all beings is the best.
shots.B06C030S01H03: Arjuna says the restless, strong and stubborn mind seems as hard to restrain as the wind, so he does not see how such steadiness can last.
shots.B06C030S01H04: Krishna agrees the mind is hard to master, but says it can be controlled by practice and by giving up desire.
shots.B06C030S01H05: Arjuna asks what becomes of a faithful person who fails to reach devotion and falls from both paths, and asks Krishna to remove this doubt.
shots.B06C030S02H01: Krishna says the one who falls from devotion is not lost, but is reborn in a good or wise family and continues toward perfection, and that the devotee who worships him with faith is the most devout.

B06C031.summary: Krishna explains that his nature has a lower eightfold form of earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, understanding and self-awareness, and a higher living form that sustains the universe. He is the source of all things, present in their qualities, but people are deluded by the three qualities and his illusion, so few know him truly. Those who turn to him reach him, while those who worship other gods receive only fleeting rewards.

scenes.B06C031S01: Krishna explains his lower and higher natures, his presence in all things, the illusion that hides him, the classes of worshippers, and who truly reaches him.

shots.B06C031S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter VII.
shots.B06C031S01H02: Krishna offers to explain knowledge and experience fully, describes his lower eightfold nature and higher living nature, names himself as the essence of many things such as water, light, the sacred syllable Om and the seed of all beings, explains that the three qualities and his illusion hide him, and says few know him, the four kinds of worshippers, and that those who worship other gods gain only what fades while his devotees come to him.

B06C032.summary: Arjuna asks Krishna to define Brahman, the self, action and the other terms, and asks how the self-restrained can be known at the hour of death. Krishna answers that Brahman is supreme and indestructible, and that whoever remembers him at death goes to him. He describes meditation at the moment of death, with the breath held between the brows and the sacred syllable Om uttered, and explains the cycles of Brahman's day and night and the two paths, the bright path with no return and the dark path that leads back to rebirth.

scenes.B06C032S01: Arjuna asks about Brahman, the self and the hour of death, and Krishna explains remembering him at death, the cycles of time and the two paths.

shots.B06C032S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter VIII.
shots.B06C032S01H02: Arjuna asks what Brahman, the self, action and the other terms mean, and how the self-restrained are to be known at the time of death.
shots.B06C032S01H03: Krishna explains that Brahman is supreme and indestructible, that whoever remembers him at death goes to him, that the meditator who holds the breath between the brows and utters Om reaches the highest goal, that the worlds below him are subject to rebirth, that Brahman's day and night are cycles that bring creatures forth and dissolve them, and that the bright and dark paths lead, one to no return and one back to rebirth, and that the knower of these paths is not deluded.

B06C033.summary: Krishna calls his teaching the royal knowledge and royal mystery, and says he pervades all things while not being bound by them. He describes how he creates and dissolves creatures in cycles, and how those who worship him with devotion are cared for, even when they worship other gods without knowing it. He declares that devotion is open to all, including women, Vaisyas and Sudras, and urges Arjuna to fix his mind on him.

scenes.B06C033S01: Krishna reveals the royal mystery of his presence in all things, the cycles of creation, and the open door of devotion to all who turn to him.

shots.B06C033S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter IX.
shots.B06C033S01H02: Krishna reveals the royal knowledge and mystery, says he pervades the universe while not being bound by it, describes the cycles of creation and dissolution, names himself as the sacrifice, offering, father and mother of the world, says even those who worship other gods without knowing it worship him, and says devotion is open to all, including the sinful, women, Vaisyas and Sudras, urging Arjuna to be devoted.

B06C034.summary: Krishna reveals that he is the source of the gods and great sages, so that they do not know his origin, and that whoever knows him as the unborn Lord is freed from sin. Arjuna asks him to describe his divine powers, and Krishna lists many of his manifestations, from Vishnu and Ganga to the Himalaya and the sacred syllable Om. He concludes that every glorious thing is only a fragment of his power, and that he upholds the whole universe with a part of himself.

scenes.B06C034S01: Krishna declares that he is the source of gods and sages, Arjuna praises him and asks for his powers, and Krishna lists his many manifestations.

shots.B06C034S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter X.
shots.B06C034S01H02: Krishna says he will speak his words for Arjuna's good, explains that the gods and sages cannot know his origin because he is their source, that whoever knows him is freed from sin, and that the qualities of creatures and the seven great sages and Manus come from him.
shots.B06C034S01H03: Arjuna praises Krishna as the supreme Brahma and the unborn Lord, and asks him to describe his divine powers, since he never tires of hearing them.
shots.B06C034S01H04: Krishna lists his manifestations among the gods, the Vedas, the mountains, the rivers, the animals, the sacred syllable Om, Death and Time, and says that everything glorious is born from a fragment of his power.

B06C035.summary: Arjuna says that Krishna's teaching has dispelled his delusion and asks to see his true, sovereign form. Krishna grants him divine sight, and Arjuna sees a vast cosmic form with countless faces and weapons, in which warriors rush into Krishna's flaming mouths. Krishna reveals himself as Time, the destroyer, tells Arjuna to fight as his instrument, and then returns to his gentle human form, saying that only devotion can truly reach him.

scenes.B06C035S01: Arjuna asks to see Krishna's true form, and Krishna grants him divine sight to behold the universal form.
scenes.B06C035S02: Krishna reveals himself as Time and the destroyer, Arjuna praises and fears him, and Krishna returns to his gentle form.
scenes.B06C035S03: Arjuna regains his composure, and Krishna explains that only devotion can reveal him.

shots.B06C035S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter XI.
shots.B06C035S01H02: Arjuna says the teaching has dispelled his delusion and asks Krishna to show him his sovereign and eternal form.
shots.B06C035S01H03: Krishna tells Arjuna to behold his many divine forms, the gods and the whole universe, and says that Arjuna cannot see him with ordinary eyes, so he gives him celestial sight.
shots.B06C035S01H04: Sanjaya describes Krishna's vast form, with many faces, weapons and ornaments, shining like a thousand suns and holding the whole divided universe, before which Arjuna bows in amazement.
shots.B06C035S01H05: Arjuna describes the form, with its endless arms, eyes and mouths, the sun and moon as eyes and fire as its mouth, and says the worlds tremble as warriors rush into its terrible mouths.
shots.B06C035S02H01: Krishna declares that he is Death and the destroyer of the worlds, that the warriors are already slain, and that Arjuna should fight and be only the instrument.
shots.B06C035S02H02: Sanjaya says Arjuna, trembling and with joined hands, bows and speaks again in fear.
shots.B06C035S02H03: Arjuna praises Krishna at length, begs pardon for past familiarity, and asks him to show again his ordinary four-armed form.
shots.B06C035S02H04: Krishna says that this form was shown to Arjuna alone by his own power, that no one else could see it through the Vedas or austerities, and tells him to be free of fear.
shots.B06C035S02H05: Sanjaya says that Krishna shows his gentle form again and comforts the frightened Arjuna.
shots.B06C035S03H01: Arjuna says that seeing Krishna's gentle human form has restored his right mind.
shots.B06C035S03H02: Krishna says that this form is hard to see, that even the gods long for it, and that he can be known and reached only through devotion to him alone, free of attachment and enmity.
shots.B06C035S03H03: Section heading marking the start of Section XXXVI.

B06C036.summary: Arjuna asks whether those who worship Krishna in personal form or those who meditate on the unmanifest are the best devotees. Krishna answers that those who fix their minds on him with faith are the most devoted, though the unmanifest path is harder. He offers to rescue such devotees and lays out a graded path for those who cannot manage fully, and he ends by describing the qualities of the devotees he loves most, who are free from hatred, content, steady and detached.

scenes.B06C036S01: Arjuna asks which devotees are best, and Krishna explains the path of personal devotion, the harder path of the unmanifest, and the qualities of those he loves.

shots.B06C036S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter XII.
shots.B06C036S01H02: Arjuna asks which worshippers are best acquainted with devotion, those who adore Krishna constantly or those who meditate on the unmanifest and immutable.
shots.B06C036S01H03: Krishna says those who fix their minds on him with supreme faith are the most devoted, that the unmanifest path is harder, that he rescues those who give him their minds and actions, that those unable to do this can practise steady devotion, act for him, or give up the fruits of action for peace, and that the devotees he loves are free from hatred, equal in pleasure and pain, content, steady and detached.

B06C037.summary: Krishna explains that the body is the field and the embodied self is its knower, and he lists the elements, qualities and virtues that make up the field and true knowledge. He describes the supreme Brahman as present everywhere, beyond the senses, and the light of all luminaries. He ends by saying that nature and spirit are both without beginning, that nature produces all the qualities while spirit only witnesses them, and that one who sees this is freed.

scenes.B06C037S01: Krishna explains the field and its knower, the virtues that make up true knowledge, the supreme Brahman, and the difference between nature and spirit.

shots.B06C037S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter XIII.
shots.B06C037S01H02: Krishna explains that the body is the field and the self is its knower, lists the elements, senses and qualities of the field, names the virtues that make up true knowledge, describes the supreme Brahman as everywhere and beyond the senses, and explains that nature and spirit are both without beginning, that nature produces all qualities while spirit witnesses them, and that one who sees the Lord equal in all beings is freed.

B06C038.summary: Krishna says he will teach again the supreme knowledge by which sages have reached perfection, and that the three qualities of nature, goodness, passion and darkness, bind the embodied soul. Each quality shapes a person's death, rebirth and reward, and a soul that sees the qualities as the only agents and rises above them attains immortality. Arjuna asks how such a person behaves, and Krishna describes his even-mindedness and his exclusive devotion.

scenes.B06C038S01: Krishna teaches how the three qualities bind the soul and how to transcend them, and he describes the person who has risen above them when Arjuna asks.

shots.B06C038S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter XIV.
shots.B06C038S01H02: Krishna says he will teach the supreme knowledge again, that the great Brahma is his womb and he the seed-giving father of all beings, that goodness, passion and darkness bind the soul, and how each quality shapes the next birth and the fruit of action, ending with the soul that transcends the three qualities and reaches immortality.
shots.B06C038S01H03: Arjuna asks what marks a person who has passed beyond the three qualities, and how such a person conducts himself.
shots.B06C038S01H04: Krishna describes this person as unmoved by light, activity or delusion, equal in pleasure and pain, praise and blame, and friend and foe, who worships him with exclusive devotion and is fit to enter the nature of Brahma.

B06C039.summary: Krishna describes the eternal fig tree, with roots above and branches below and leaves that are the Vedas, which must be cut down with detachment so that one can seek the supreme seat that no one returns from. He says that the individual soul is an eternal part of himself, carried from body to body like scent on the wind, and that he is the light in the sun, moon and fire. He identifies himself as the Supreme Person, beyond both the perishable and the imperishable, and says that whoever knows him worships him fully.

scenes.B06C039S01: Krishna describes the eternal fig tree of the world, the soul as his part, his presence in the light of the world, and his supreme nature beyond the perishable and imperishable.

shots.B06C039S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter XV.
shots.B06C039S01H02: Krishna describes the eternal fig tree whose leaves are the Vedas, says it must be cut with detachment to reach the supreme seat, explains that the soul is his eternal part carried between bodies with the senses, that he is the light in the sun, moon and fire and the warmth of digestion, the source of memory and knowledge, and the Supreme Person beyond the perishable and imperishable.

B06C040.summary: Krishna lists the divine qualities, such as fearlessness, purity, self-control, compassion and humility, which lead to liberation, and contrasts them with the demonic qualities of hypocrisy, pride, anger and ignorance, which lead to bondage. He describes demonic people who deny moral order, pursue endless desires, and are cast down into hell. He names lust, anger and greed as the three gates to hell and tells Arjuna that scripture should guide what he does.

scenes.B06C040S01: Krishna sets the divine and demonic qualities side by side, describes the demonic people and their fall, and names the three gates of hell.

shots.B06C040S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter XVI.
shots.B06C040S01H02: Krishna lists divine qualities that lead to liberation and demonic qualities that lead to bondage, describes demonic people who deny truth and moral order and chase endless desires, names lust, anger and greed as the three gates to hell, and says that scripture should guide what one does.

B06C041.summary: Arjuna asks whether the worship of those who act outside the scriptures, but with faith, is of goodness, passion or darkness. Krishna explains that faith and everything else, including food, sacrifice, penance and gifts, come in these three forms according to a person's nature. He ends by naming Brahma as OM, TAT and SAT, and says that any act done without faith counts for nothing here or hereafter.

scenes.B06C041S01: Arjuna asks about faith outside scripture, and Krishna explains the three kinds of faith, food, sacrifice, penance and gifts, ending with the sacred words OM, TAT and SAT.

shots.B06C041S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter XVII.
shots.B06C041S01H02: Arjuna asks whether the state of those who worship with faith apart from the scriptures is one of goodness, passion or darkness.
shots.B06C041S01H03: Krishna says faith comes in three kinds that follow each person's nature, sorts worship, food, sacrifice, penance of body, speech and mind, and gifts into the three qualities, names Brahma as OM, TAT and SAT, and says that any act done without faith is worthless here and hereafter.

B06C042.summary: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain the true nature of renunciation and abandonment. Krishna distinguishes three kinds of each by quality, teaches the causes of action, the three qualities of knowledge, action, agent and understanding, and the natural duties of each social class, saying one's own duty is better even when imperfect. He then urges Arjuna to surrender everything to him and promises deliverance, and Arjuna says his delusion is gone and he will act as Krishna bids. Sanjaya closes by saying that he heard this dialogue through Vyasa's favour, and that where Krishna and Partha are, there is victory and justice.

scenes.B06C042S01: Arjuna asks about renunciation, Krishna explains the three qualities of action, knowledge and duty, urges surrender to him, and Arjuna accepts; Sanjaya then closes the dialogue.
scenes.B06C042S02: A closing marker that ends the Bhagavad Gita.

shots.B06C042S01H01: Heading naming the start of Bhagavad Gita Chapter XVIII.
shots.B06C042S01H02: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain the true nature of renunciation and of abandonment.
shots.B06C042S01H03: Krishna explains that renouncing desired acts and their fruit is abandonment, that sacrifice, gifts and penance should still be done without attachment, sorts renunciation, knowledge, action, agent, understanding and happiness into three qualities, sets out the natural duties of each social class and says one's own duty is better even if imperfect, and then urges Arjuna to surrender to him as his devoted friend and promises to free him from sin.
shots.B06C042S01H04: Arjuna says his delusion is destroyed, his memory has returned, his doubts are gone, and he will do as Krishna asks.
shots.B06C042S01H05: Sanjaya says he heard this wonderful dialogue through Vyasa's favour, rejoices in recalling it and the form of Hari, and says that wherever Krishna and Partha are, there is prosperity, victory and justice.
shots.B06C042S02H01: Closing marker, End of the Bhagavad Gita.

B06C043.summary: Yudhishthira puts down his armour and weapons and walks on foot toward the Kaurava elders, followed by his brothers and Krishna, while the Kaurava side mocks him as frightened. He asks Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and Salya for leave and blessings to fight, and each grants it while confessing that he is bound to the Kauravas by their wealth and must fight for them. Krishna then tries to win Karna to the Pandava side, Karna refuses out of loyalty to Duryodhana, and Yuyutsu, a son of Dhritarashtra, joins the Pandavas amid general praise.

scenes.B06C043S01: Yudhishthira walks unarmed toward the Kaurava elders, and his brothers question him as he goes.
scenes.B06C043S02: Yudhishthira salutes Bhishma, who grants him leave to fight and says he is bound to the Kauravas by their wealth.
scenes.B06C043S03: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how he can be defeated, and Bhishma says no one can beat him while his time has not come.
scenes.B06C043S04: Yudhishthira asks Drona for leave and blessing, and Drona grants them, confessing that he too is bound to the Kauravas by wealth.
scenes.B06C043S05: Drona tells Yudhishthira that he can be killed only when he lays down his arms, and Yudhishthira goes on to Kripa.
scenes.B06C043S06: Yudhishthira seeks leave from Kripa and Salya, who both grant it while saying they must fight for the Kauravas.
scenes.B06C043S07: Yudhishthira asks Salya to weaken Karna, Salya agrees, and Krishna goes to Karna to urge him to switch sides.
scenes.B06C043S08: Karna refuses to desert Duryodhana, Yuyutsu joins the Pandavas, and both armies prepare for battle.

shots.B06C043S01H01: After Arjuna takes up his bow again, the armies shout and the gods and sages gather to watch; Yudhishthira puts down his armour and weapons and walks on foot toward the enemy, with his brothers and Krishna behind him.
shots.B06C043S01H02: Arjuna asks Yudhishthira what he means by walking unarmed toward the enemy and leaving his brothers behind.
shots.B06C043S01H03: Bhima asks where his brother is going without his armour and weapons, towards the armoured foe, and leaving his brothers.
shots.B06C043S01H04: Nakula says he is troubled with fear to see his eldest brother going this way and asks where he is headed.
shots.B06C043S01H05: Sahadeva asks why Yudhishthira is heading toward the foe when the terrible enemy divisions are so near.
shots.B06C043S02H01: Krishna says Yudhishthira means to honour his elders before the fight, and the Kaurava warriors mock him as a coward, until Yudhishthira reaches Bhishma and seizes his feet.
shots.B06C043S02H02: Yudhishthira salutes Bhishma and asks for his permission and blessing to fight.
shots.B06C043S02H03: Bhishma says he would have cursed Yudhishthira had he not come, grants his blessing, and says he is bound to the Kauravas by their wealth and must fight for them.
shots.B06C043S02H04: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to think of his welfare from day to day, even while he fights for the Kauravas.
shots.B06C043S02H05: Bhishma says he will fight for Yudhishthira's foes and asks what else he wants to say.
shots.B06C043S03H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how he could be vanquished in battle, and asks for any advice that would help him.
shots.B06C043S03H02: Bhishma says he sees no one who can defeat him in battle while he fights.
shots.B06C043S03H03: Yudhishthira asks how Bhishma's own death could be brought about by his foes.
shots.B06C043S03H04: Bhishma says he sees no one who can vanquish him, and that the time of his death has not yet come.
shots.B06C043S03H05: Sanjaya says Yudhishthira accepts the words, salutes Bhishma again, and goes on through the army to Drona's chariot.
shots.B06C043S04H01: Yudhishthira asks Drona how he may fight without sin and vanquish his foes with Drona's permission.
shots.B06C043S04H02: Drona grants permission and blessing, says he is bound by the Kauravas' wealth, and asks what Yudhishthira wants.
shots.B06C043S04H03: Yudhishthira asks Drona to pray for his victory and advise him for his good, while Drona fights for the Kauravas.
shots.B06C043S04H04: Drona says victory is certain for Yudhishthira because Hari is his counsellor, and that victory goes wherever righteousness and Krishna are.
shots.B06C043S04H05: Yudhishthira asks Drona how he could be vanquished, since he is invincible.
shots.B06C043S05H01: Drona says that victory cannot be Yudhishthira's while he is fighting, and urges him to seek Drona's speedy death.
shots.B06C043S05H02: Yudhishthira asks Drona to name the means of his death, and salutes him.
shots.B06C043S05H03: Drona says no foe can slay him while he fights with wrath and arrows, only when he sets down his weapons and withdraws into meditation, which he will do if he hears something very disagreeable.
shots.B06C043S05H04: Sanjaya says Yudhishthira honours Drona and goes on to Kripa.
shots.B06C043S05H05: Yudhishthira asks for Drona's leave to fight without sin and vanquish his foes.
shots.B06C043S06H01: Kripa says he would have cursed Yudhishthira had he not come, that he is bound to the Kauravas by their wealth, and that he must speak like a eunuch and fight for them.
shots.B06C043S06H02: Yudhishthira begins to speak but, greatly agitated, falls silent.
shots.B06C043S06H03: Sanjaya says Kripa understands what Yudhishthira meant, says he cannot be slain, promises to pray for his victory, and Yudhishthira goes on to Salya.
shots.B06C043S06H04: Yudhishthira asks Salya for leave to fight without sin and vanquish his foes.
shots.B06C043S06H05: Salya grants leave and blessing, says he is bound to the Kauravas by their wealth, and asks what Yudhishthira desires.
shots.B06C043S07H01: Yudhishthira asks Salya to think daily of his welfare and to fight as he pleases for the sake of the foe, and says this is the boon he asks.
shots.B06C043S07H02: Salya says he must fight for the Kauravas, who have bound him with their wealth, and asks what aid he can give.
shots.B06C043S07H03: Yudhishthira asks Salya to weaken the energy of Karna in battle.
shots.B06C043S07H04: Salya agrees to do so and says he will watch over Yudhishthira's victory.
shots.B06C043S07H05: Sanjaya says Yudhishthira and his brothers leave the Kaurava line, and Krishna goes to Karna and asks him to join the Pandavas until Bhishma is slain.
shots.B06C043S08H01: Karna says he will not displease Duryodhana, for whom he has given up his life, so Krishna returns to the Pandavas; Yudhishthira calls for allies, and Yuyutsu, a son of Dhritarashtra, offers to fight for them.
shots.B06C043S08H02: Yudhishthira accepts Yuyutsu's offer, saying the Kaurava line rests on him and the wrathful Duryodhana will not live long.
shots.B06C043S08H03: Yuyutsu leaves the Kauravas for the Pandavas, the armies counter-array, the kings praise the Pandavas' nobility, and onlookers of every kind weep as they witness it.

B06C044.summary: Dhritarashtra asks who struck the first blow when the two armies were drawn up. Sanjaya describes the rush of Dussasana and Bhishma against the Pandavas, led by Bhima, and the awful roar that frightens Dhritarashtra's sons. The fierce first encounter is then described, with the Kaurava princes surrounding Bhima, the Pandava warriors striking back, and Bhishma shining above all the rest.

scenes.B06C044S01: Dhritarashtra asks who struck first, and Sanjaya describes the first clash of the two armies, led by Bhishma and Bhima.

shots.B06C044S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks who struck the first blow, the Kurus or the Pandavas, once the two armies were arrayed.
shots.B06C044S01H02: Sanjaya describes Dussasana and Bhishma advancing with the Kaurava troops and the Pandavas advancing under Bhima, the deafening uproar, Bhima's roars that frighten the Kaurava sons, the Kaurava princes surrounding him with arrows and the Pandava warriors striking back, and Bhishma shining above the countless host.

B06C045.summary: The battle begins in earnest on the forenoon of the terrible day, and Sanjaya describes a long series of single combats across the field. Bhishma and Arjuna, Satyaki and Kritavarman, Abhimanyu and Vrihadbala, Bhima and Duryodhana, the twins Nakula and Sahadeva, Yudhishthira and the king of Madra, and many others fight fiercely, until the whole field becomes a confused melee that the onlookers compare to a war of gods and demons.

scenes.B06C045S01: The battle opens with a huge uproar and a series of single combats between the leading warriors of both sides, until the fighting becomes a confused melee.

shots.B06C045S01H01: Sanjaya describes the uproar at the start of the battle, then the paired duels of Bhishma and Arjuna, Satyaki and Kritavarman, Abhimanyu and Vrihadbala, Bhima and Duryodhana, Nakula and Dussasana, Sahadeva and Durmukha, Yudhishthira and the king of Madra, Dhrishtadyumna and Drona, and many other pairs of warriors, until the melee becomes so confused that nothing can be discerned.

B06C046.summary: Sanjaya describes the fighting among the foot soldiers, where men lose all regard for one another, and sires, sons, brothers and friends kill each other. Elephants, horses, chariots and foot soldiers are shattered in the chaos, and the wounded cry out for kin and water while some brave men endure in silence. Under this assault the Pandava divisions begin to waver before Bhishma, who shines on his silver-standard chariot.

scenes.B06C046S01: Sanjaya describes the slaughter among foot soldiers, elephants, horses and chariots, where kin kill one another, and the Pandava divisions begin to waver before Bhishma.

shots.B06C046S01H01: Sanjaya describes the frenzied fighting among foot soldiers, where kin fail to recognise each other, elephants and horses are slaughtered, the wounded call for their kin and for water, and some warriors bear their pain silently, until the Pandava divisions waver before Bhishma, who shines on his silver chariot.

B06C047.summary: Sanjaya describes how Bhishma, protected by Durmukha, Kritavarman, Kripa, Salya and Vivinsati, cuts through the Pandava ranks. Abhimanyu duels with Bhishma and his guards, knocks down Bhishma's palmyra standard, and is cheered by the Pandavas. Sweta, son of Virata, then charges Salya until seven Kaurava champions hold him back, and Duryodhana and Bhishma rescue Salya.

scenes.B06C047S01: Bhishma's guards press forward, Abhimanyu fells Bhishma's standard, and Sweta's charge against Salya is halted and Salya rescued.

shots.B06C047S01H01: Sanjaya tells how Bhishma, guarded by five Kaurava champions, cuts through the Pandava ranks, how Abhimanyu duels with him and cuts down his palmyra standard, how Bhima's standard also falls to Bhishma, how Salya kills Uttara's elephant, and how Sweta is stopped by seven Kaurava champions until Duryodhana and Bhishma rescue Salya.

B06C048.summary: Dhritarashtra asks what the two armies did when Sweta charged Salya, and Sanjaya describes a great slaughter in which Bhishma stands alone among the Kauravas. Bhishma and Sweta duel, breaking each other's bows and standards, and a celestial voice tells Bhishma that his hour of victory has come. Bhishma kills Sweta with a shaft, the Pandavas grieve and the Kauravas rejoice, and at nightfall both armies withdraw.

scenes.B06C048S01: Dhritarashtra asks what happened when Sweta charged Salya, and Sanjaya describes the duel between Bhishma and Sweta, Sweta's death and the nightfall withdrawal.

shots.B06C048S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks what the Kauravas and Pandavas did when Sweta advanced on Salya's chariot, and what Bhishma did in response.
shots.B06C048S01H02: Sanjaya describes the great slaughter around Sweta, the Kaurava warriors fleeing and leaving Bhishma alone, the duel in which bows and standards fall and Bhishma's chariot is destroyed by Sweta's mace, the celestial voice that marks Bhishma's hour, Sweta's death by Bhishma's shaft, the grief of the Pandavas, the joy of the Kauravas, and the withdrawal of both armies at nightfall.

B06C049.summary: Dhritarashtra, having heard of Sweta's death, asks what the Pandavas did next, reproaches Duryodhana for provoking the war, and fears what Arjuna will do in his anger. Sanjaya tells him to own his own part, then describes Sankha's attack on Salya, Arjuna's stand against Bhishma in his defence, and Bhishma's rout of the Panchala and Matsya troops until the Pandavas withdraw at sunset.

scenes.B06C049S01: Dhritarashtra questions Sanjaya about the Pandava response and his own guilt, and Sanjaya describes the fighting of the day, with Bhishma routing the Pandava forces until nightfall.

shots.B06C049S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks how the Pandavas and Panchalas reacted to Sweta's death, reproaches Duryodhana for provoking the war, says Bhishma, Drona and others never wanted it, and fears what Arjuna will do in his wrath.
shots.B06C049S01H02: Sanjaya tells the king to accept his own share of blame, describes Sankha's charge on Salya and Arjuna's stand before Bhishma, then Bhishma's slaughter of the Panchala and Matsya troops and of Drupada's army, and the Pandavas withdrawing for the night as the sun sets.

B06C050.summary: After the first day's fighting, Yudhishthira goes to Krishna in despair at Bhishma's power and says he would rather retire to the forest than see his kings destroyed, while complaining that Arjuna seems indifferent. Krishna comforts him and Yudhishthira makes Dhrishtadyumna commander of the army, who vows to slay Bhishma and Drona. Dhrishtadyumna then forms the Krauncharuma array, with Arjuna in the van and Drupada at its head, ready for the next morning's battle.

scenes.B06C050S01: Yudhishthira laments Bhishma's power before Krishna, is comforted, appoints Dhrishtadyumna commander, and the Pandava army is drawn up in the Krauncharuma array for the next day.

shots.B06C050S01H01: Yudhishthira goes to Krishna after the first day, lamenting that Bhishma consumes his army like fire, that he would rather go to the forest than see kings slain, that Arjuna seems indifferent while Bhima fights alone, and asks Krishna what can be done.
shots.B06C050S01H02: Krishna comforts Yudhishthira, Yudhishthira makes Dhrishtadyumna commander and compares him to Kartikeya, Dhrishtadyumna vows to slay Bhishma and Drona, and at dawn he forms the Krauncharuma array with Arjuna in the van, Drupada at the head, Virata guarding the rear, and the army's banners shining.
shots.B06C050S01H03: Section heading marking the start of Section LI.

B06C051.summary: Duryodhana, seeing the Pandava Krauncha array, urges Bhishma, Drona and the other commanders to protect the front, and arranges his own army with Bhishma at its head, Drona and Ashvatthama in support, and Duryodhana's brothers and allied kings on the flanks and rear. Both sides then blow their conches, and the two armies advance to battle once more.

scenes.B06C051S01: Duryodhana arranges his own army against the Pandava array, and both sides sound their conches before advancing.

shots.B06C051S01H01: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana's speech to his commanders, the Kaurava formation with Bhishma at its head, Drona behind him, Duryodhana and his brothers in the centre, allied kings on the flanks and rear, and both sides blowing their conches as the armies advance to battle once again.

B06C052.summary: Duryodhana orders his army to attack, and Bhishma's arrows drive back the Pandava divisions. Arjuna asks Krishna to drive him straight at Bhishma, vowing to slay him, and Bhishma wounds many warriors, including Krishna. Duryodhana then urges Bhishma to kill Arjuna because Karna refuses to fight, and Bhishma goes after him in a duel that the gods watch with wonder, since neither man gains the advantage.

scenes.B06C052S01: Dhritarashtra asks how the battle began, Duryodhana orders the attack, and Bhishma and Arjuna fight a long duel that the gods regard as unmatched.

shots.B06C052S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks how the foremost warriors began to strike once the two armies were arrayed.
shots.B06C052S01H02: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana ordering the attack, Bhishma's arrows driving back the Pandava divisions, Arjuna asking Krishna to drive him at Bhishma and vowing to slay him, Bhishma wounding many warriors including Krishna, Duryodhana urging Bhishma to kill Arjuna because Karna will not fight, and the long duel between Bhishma and Arjuna, which neither wins and which the gods watch in wonder.

B06C053.summary: Dhritarashtra asks how Drona and Dhrishtadyumna fought, and says that fate seems stronger than effort, since even Bhishma could not escape Arjuna. Sanjaya describes the duel in which Drona breaks Dhrishtadyumna's bow, chariot and steeds, and in which Dhrishtadyumna's mace and dart are also broken. When Dhrishtadyumna charges on foot with shield and sword, Bhima comes to his rescue, and Duryodhana sends the Kalingas against Bhima.

scenes.B06C053S01: Dhritarashtra asks about the duel between Drona and Dhrishtadyumna, and Sanjaya describes Drona's victories, Dhrishtadyumna's defiance, and Bhima's rescue.

shots.B06C053S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks how Drona and Dhrishtadyumna fought, and says fate seems stronger than effort, since even Bhishma could not escape Arjuna.
shots.B06C053S01H02: Sanjaya describes Drona breaking Dhrishtadyumna's bow, charioteer and steeds, cutting down his dart and mace, Dhrishtadyumna charging on foot with shield and sword, Drona holding him off, Bhima rushing to rescue him, and Duryodhana sending the Kalingas against Bhima.

B06C054.summary: Urged on by Duryodhana, the Kalinga king and his allies attack Bhima, but Bhima slays the king's son Sakradeva with a mace and cuts down the king's elephant and many of his men in a rampage. Dhrishtadyumna and Satyaki come to his aid, and Satyaki kills Bhishma's charioteer, forcing Bhishma to be carried from the field. The Kalinga army is broken and Bhima stands triumphant in the middle of the troops.

scenes.B06C054S01: Dhritarashtra asks how the Kalinga king fought Bhima, and Sanjaya describes Bhima's rampage through the Kalinga forces and the rescue by Dhrishtadyumna and Satyaki.

shots.B06C054S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks how the Kalinga king, urged on by his son, fought against Bhima, who wanders the field with his mace like Death himself.
shots.B06C054S01H02: Sanjaya describes the Kalinga attack on Bhima, his slaying of Sakradeva with a mace, the beheading of the king's elephant, his sword rampage among the Kalingas and their allies, the Kalinga flight, Dhrishtadyumna and Satyaki joining the fight, and Satyaki felling Bhishma's charioteer so that Bhishma is carried from the field.

B06C055.summary: In the afternoon Dhrishtadyumna fights Drona's son, Salya and Kripa, while Abhimanyu duels with Duryodhana's son Lakshmana, breaking his bow before Duryodhana comes to his son's aid. Arjuna then rushes to rescue Abhimanyu, and the Kaurava kings charge him, but his arrows scatter them and fill the field with broken weapons. Bhishma sees the army routed and orders its withdrawal as the sun sets.

scenes.B06C055S01: Dhrishtadyumna, Abhimanyu and Arjuna fight the Kaurava leaders, Arjuna scatters the army, and Bhishma withdraws the Kaurava forces at sunset.

shots.B06C055S01H01: Sanjaya describes Dhrishtadyumna killing the horses of Drona's son and attacking Salya, Kripa and Drona's son, Abhimanyu's duel with Lakshmana, Duryodhana's rush to his son's side, Arjuna's rescue of Abhimanyu, the Kaurava kings' charge, the broken weapons strewn across the field, and Bhishma's order to withdraw as the sun sets.

B06C056.summary: At dawn Bhishma forms the Kaurava army in the shape of a Garuda, the eagle, with himself at its beak, Drona and Kritavarman at its eyes, and Duryodhana on its back. Arjuna answers with a half-moon formation, with Bhima on one horn, Dhrishtadyumna and Sikhandin in the middle, Yudhishthira with his elephants, and Krishna guarding the other horn. The two armies then clash in a roar that reaches the heavens.

scenes.B06C056S01: Bhishma forms the Garuda array, Arjuna answers with a half-moon array, and the armies clash at dawn.

shots.B06C056S01H01: Sanjaya describes Bhishma's Garuda formation with its commanders at each part, Arjuna's half-moon counter-array with Bhima on the right horn and Krishna on the left, the Pandava leaders placed in between, and the armies' clash with its uproar reaching the heavens.

B06C057.summary: Once the armies are drawn up, Arjuna cuts down the leaders of the Kaurava car divisions, and the fighting becomes a general melee of cars, elephants, cavalry and infantry, with the field strewn with broken weapons and bodies. Bhishma, Drona, Jayadratha, Sakuni and others break the Pandava ranks in turn, while Bhima, Ghatotkacha and the sons of Draupadi grind down the Kaurava host. The chapter ends with Duryodhana, Abhimanyu and Satyaki joining the fight in a new, fierce round of combat.

scenes.B06C057S01: Arjuna cuts down Kaurava car leaders, the armies fight in a general melee, and both sides push and break each other's ranks.

shots.B06C057S01H01: Sanjaya describes Arjuna's slaughter of the Kaurava car leaders, the general melee of cars, elephants, cavalry and foot soldiers across a field strewn with broken weapons and bodies, Bhishma, Drona, Jayadratha and Sakuni breaking the Pandava ranks, Bhima, Ghatotkacha and the sons of Draupadi grinding the Kaurava host, and Duryodhana, Abhimanyu and Satyaki joining the fight.

B06C058.summary: Kings surround Arjuna with a storm of weapons, while Satyaki and Abhimanyu fight Sakuni's forces. Bhima wounds Duryodhana in the chest, and when Duryodhana swoons and is carried away, the Kaurava army flees, leaving Bhishma and Drona unable to stop it. Duryodhana rallies his men and rebukes Bhishma for sparing the Pandavas, and Bhishma vows to check them alone, so both sides sound their conches for the next round.

scenes.B06C058S01: Kings attack Arjuna, Bhima wounds Duryodhana and routs his army, and Duryodhana rebukes Bhishma, who vows to fight alone.

shots.B06C058S01H01: Sanjaya describes the kings surrounding Arjuna with a storm of weapons, Sakuni's forces cutting up Satyaki's car until he and Abhimanyu share one car, Drona and Bhishma pressing Yudhishthira, Bhima's arrow wounding Duryodhana so that he swoons and is carried away and his army flees, Arjuna scattering the Kauravas, Duryodhana rallying them and rebuking Bhishma, and Bhishma's vow to check the Pandavas alone, with both sides sounding their conches.

B06C059.summary: Stung by Duryodhana's taunts, Bhishma charges into the Pandava army, slaughtering their warriors so swiftly that he seems to be everywhere at once, and the Pandava host breaks. Krishna urges Arjuna to strike Bhishma, and their duel leaves Krishna and Arjuna pierced by arrows. Krishna leaps down with his discus to kill Bhishma, who invites the blow, but Arjuna holds Krishna back, and then Arjuna unleashes the Indra weapon, making a river of blood, until the Kauravas withdraw at nightfall lamenting their losses.

scenes.B06C059S01: Bhishma storms the Pandava army, Krishna and Arjuna face him in a duel, Arjuna holds back Krishna's attack on Bhishma, and Arjuna's Indra weapon brings carnage until nightfall.

shots.B06C059S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks what Bhishma did against the Pandavas after his dreadful vow in battle, and what the Panchalas did in response.
shots.B06C059S01H02: Sanjaya describes Bhishma's charge through the Pandava army with arrows that cut down warriors and make him seem multiplied, the Pandava rout, Krishna urging Arjuna to strike Bhishma, their arrowy duel in which Krishna's discus is raised and Arjuna holds him back and vows to fight, Arjuna's Indra weapon that fills the field with carnage and a river of blood, and the Kaurava withdrawal at nightfall with praise of Arjuna's feat.

B06C060.summary: On the next morning Bhishma leads the Kaurava army forward, surrounded by Drona, Duryodhana, Jayadratha and other princes, against Arjuna's array. The two sides clash amid a storm of dust, conches and falling warriors. Bhishma then turns on Arjuna, and their arrowy single combat is watched by both armies as Abhimanyu charges deep into the Kaurava host.

scenes.B06C060S01: The third day opens with Bhishma leading the Kaurava army against Arjuna, the armies clash, and Bhishma and Arjuna duel while Abhimanyu attacks the Kaurava ranks.

shots.B06C060S01H01: Sanjaya describes Bhishma advancing with the Kaurava princes around him, the glittering banners and elephants, Arjuna's array with Krishna as charioteer, the blare of drums and conches, and the clash in which the sky is covered with dust and warriors, horsemen and elephants fall in heaps.
shots.B06C060S01H02: Bhishma turns to attack Arjuna, Abhimanyu charges into the Kaurava host in the meantime, and Arjuna answers Bhishma's arrows with a shower of his own while both armies watch the single combat between the two champions.

B06C061.summary: Abhimanyu fights alone against Drona's son, Bhurisravas, Chitrasena and other warriors, and the Kaurava princes surround him. Dhrishtadyumna comes to his rescue, and in a duel Dhrishtadyumna kills Samyamani's son with a mace, provoking Samyamani to attack Dhrishtadyumna in turn. Salya joins the attack on Dhrishtadyumna, and a new round of fighting begins.

scenes.B06C061S01: Abhimanyu battles the Kaurava princes, Dhrishtadyumna rescues him, Samyamani's son is killed, and Samyamani and Salya attack Dhrishtadyumna.

shots.B06C061S01H01: Sanjaya describes Abhimanyu's stand against Drona's son, Bhurisravas, Chitrasena and Samyamani's son, the Trigarta, Madra and Kekaya princes surrounding him and his father, Dhrishtadyumna's rescue, the duel in which Dhrishtadyumna's mace kills Samyamani's son, Samyamani's fierce attack on Dhrishtadyumna, and Salya striking Dhrishtadyumna in the chest.
